formalObservation.Composition:
This is the most densely populated composition in the selected final group.

Major visual units:

- large form in upper-left
- large rectangular/rounded figure in upper-right
- central horizontal figure
- large lower figure occupying bottom half
- several smaller forms connecting the composition

Unlike B-010 and B-011, the composition is not primarily horizontal. It occupies almost the entire vertical field.

formalObservation.Mark-Making:
Very high density of charcoal activity:

- dense parallel hatching
- heavy contour strokes
- filled charcoal masses
- overlapping lines
- directional strokes
- lighter construction marks
- areas of repeated cross-directional texture

Outer edges of several figures are substantially darker than their interiors.
formalObservation.Visual Density:
Very High

One of the most visually dense works in the selected twelve.
formalObservation.Spatial Strategy:
Vertical / Layered / Overlapping / Enclosed

The composition builds from top to bottom. Several major forms occupy different vertical zones while overlapping or approaching one another.

Unlike B-005's segmented structure, divisions between zones are considerably less rigid.
formalObservation.Figure–Ground Relationship:
Complex.

Principal figures remain identifiable, but surrounding hatching and structural marks frequently bridge the space between them. The distinction between individual figure and surrounding field is therefore less absolute than in simpler works.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Dense vertical composition.
- Multiple large figure-like units.
- Strong repetition of circular and triangular forms.
- Organic contours coexist with rectangular structures.
- Heavy hatching creates visual continuity across separate zones.
- Scale varies substantially between figures.
- Overlap and proximity establish relationships between major figures.
- The page is treated as a unified field rather than a collection of isolated drawings.
